lessons.title: Taxes, government spending and the budget
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level Economics — government revenue and expenditure (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Define direct and indirect taxes and progressive, proportional and regressive taxes.
Describe the purposes of taxation and the government budget.
Calculate income tax, VAT and a budget balance.
reviewNotes: The VAT rate and tax bands are invented for teaching; actual Cameroonian rates are not given and must be taken from the current tax code.
Annual passing of the finance law by Parliament is stated in outline.
All prices, quantities and FCFA amounts are invented teaching figures, not real market data.
The order and depth of topics are an editorial choice to be checked against the Cameroon GCE Board O Level Economics syllabus.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Taxes
blocks.md: A **tax** is a compulsory payment to the government. **Direct taxes** are paid directly by the person or firm on whom they fall: **income tax**, **company tax**. **Indirect taxes** are placed on goods and services and paid when buying: **VAT** (value added tax) and **customs duties** on imports. Governments use taxes to raise **revenue**, to redistribute income, to discourage harmful goods and to protect local industry.

blocks.title: Progressive, proportional and regressive
blocks.md: **Progressive**: the percentage of income paid in tax rises as income rises (income tax with bands). **Proportional**: the same percentage at all incomes. **Regressive**: the percentage falls as income rises (a flat tax on a good takes more of a poor person's income). Good taxes are **fair, certain, convenient** and **cheap to collect** (the canons of taxation).

blocks.caption: An imaginary budget: spending of 78 is greater than revenue of 62, giving a deficit of 16.
blocks.alt: Two bars: revenue 62 and spending 78 in billion FCFA.

blocks.title: The government budget
blocks.md: The **budget** is the government's plan for **revenue** (taxes, income from state firms, oil and other resources, borrowing) and **expenditure** (education, health, roads, defence, wages of public workers, debt payments). If revenue is greater than spending there is a **surplus**; if smaller, a **deficit**, which is financed by borrowing at home or abroad. In Cameroon the budget is passed each year by Parliament as a finance law.

blocks.title: Frequent mistakes
blocks.md: Do not call any payment to government a tax: **fees** and **fines** are different. Indirect taxes are paid by consumers even though shops pay them to the state. A progressive tax is not the same as a **high** tax. A deficit is not the same as **national debt**: the debt is the total accumulated, the deficit is the one-year gap. Taxes can also change behaviour: high taxes may discourage work or encourage tax evasion.

blocks.title: Worked example — progressive income tax
blocks.statement: In an imaginary system the first 100 000 FCFA of yearly income is untaxed, the next 200 000 is taxed at 10 % and anything above 300 000 at 20 %. Find the tax and the average rate for an income of 400 000 FCFA.

blocks.title: Worked example — VAT and the budget
blocks.statement: A shop sells a product for 20 000 FCFA before tax and VAT is charged at 10 % (illustrative rate). Find the final price. A government expects revenue of 62 and spends 78 (billion FCFA). What is the budget balance?
steps: VAT = 20 000 × 10 ÷ 100 = 2000 FCFA, so the price is 22 000 FCFA.

exercises.source: Original exercise written for CastBridge, in the style of the curriculum
exercises.prompt: Fotso earns 200 000 FCFA a year and Njie earns 400 000 FCFA, taxed under the imaginary bands in the lesson (0 % up to 100 000, 10 % to 300 000, 20 % above).

parts.prompt: Average tax rate paid by Fotso (%)?
Is the system progressive? Give a reason.
parts.model: Yes: Fotso pays 5 % and Njie pays 10 % on average, so the average rate rises with income.
parts.explanation: Yes: Fotso pays 5 % and Njie pays 10 % on average, so the average rate rises with income.

exercises.prompt: O Level — A direct tax is one that
choices: is paid directly to the government by the person or firm on whom it is placed
is included in the price of goods
exercises.explanation: Income tax and company tax are direct taxes.

exercises.prompt: O Level — Value added tax (VAT) is an example of
exercises.explanation: It is added to the price paid on goods and services.

exercises.prompt: O Level — A progressive tax takes
choices: a smaller percentage as income rises
nothing from the poor and the rich
a larger percentage of income as income rises
exercises.explanation: The tax rate increases with income.

exercises.prompt: O Level — A budget deficit occurs when
choices: government spending is greater than its revenue
exercises.explanation: The gap must be financed by borrowing or other means.

exercises.prompt: O Level — Which is a good quality of a tax according to the canons of taxation?
choices: It costs more to collect than it earns
It is certain and fair to taxpayers
exercises.explanation: Equity, certainty, convenience and economy are the classic qualities.
